NKT A/S (NKT-DK): the start-up of two new cable lines at Karlskrona is the whole thesis

Investment memo for Richard, 14 October 2026. Share price 867 DKK on 12 October 2026 (about 116 EUR; market value about 6.2bn EUR). NKT reports Q3 2026 on 19 November 2026 and gives its first FY2027 guidance with the FY2026 results in February 2027.

Conventions. Figures are in EUR unless marked DKK. "Our model" is Viewforth's base case; "consensus" is the FactSet median of 25 September 2026. Definitions, sources and terms are in the end notes.

#0Summary: buy NKT in stages ahead of a dated, contracted earnings step

The case in one sentence.

NKT has already sold its next five years of high-voltage cable capacity at about twice the last cycle's prices, so its next two years of earnings depend on one event: whether two new extrusion lines at its Karlskrona plant in Sweden produce commercial cable around Q2 2027. The market prices that start-up as a coin toss; we put the odds at about two in three.

The seven conclusions that matter

1
NKT's demand, prices and costs are already contracted, so the only open question is when the new capacity starts.
NKT's 13.0bn EUR Transmission backlog covers about ten years of current Transmission revenue, and more than 95% of it is owed by state-backed European grid operators. Contracts signed since 2022 pass metal costs through and index other costs to inflation. New 525kV contracts are priced at 1.44m EUR per kilometre, against 0.62m in 2019-20. NKT's revenue is therefore limited by its capacity, not by demand: kilometres produced times the contracted price.
2
The earnings step from FY2026 to FY2028 is large, and most of it is mechanical.
About 75-80% of the increase in EBITDA comes from the new capacity coming on stream. The rest comes from older, lower-priced contracts finishing, which is already under way.
3
The market is not yet paying for the earnings step: NKT trades near the bottom of its own valuation range.
NKT trades at 15.9 times 24-month-forward earnings, the 21st percentile of its own ten-year range, while Prysmian and Cenergy trade at the 83rd and 92nd percentiles of theirs. The de-rating is specific to NKT: its shares are 23% below their high despite a guidance raise in August. Today's market penalises long-dated projects that consume cash, and investors doubt NKT's timing rather than lack information.
4
The return is large at the fair multiple and still positive at our more cautious multiple, so the skew is unusually favourable.
  • At the fair multiple of 30.17x (Viewforth's phase guideline): about +128% over 18 months, four-fifths of it from re-rating. Even the severe slip scenario returns about +86%.
  • At our multiple (about 19x if the plant runs): about +45% in the most likely scenario (47% probability) and about +28% probability-weighted.
  • With no re-rating (a flat 16x): about +23% in the on-time scenario, from earnings growth and dividends alone.
  • The downside is bounded at -16% to -27% (5% probability), because FY2028 earnings are contracted and the shares already sit in the bottom quarter of their range.
5
The next six months will probably bring negative-looking news, and the positive news arrives from August 2027.
NKT habitually guides low, so its first FY2027 guidance, due in February 2027, will probably sit 5-12% below consensus, and estimates for EPS and FY2027 free cash flow are likely to be cut. From August 2027 the good news arrives: first commercial cable, a likely guidance raise and positive free cash flow. Our edge is knowing this sequence, not having better information.
6
The fair multiple of 30.17x comes from Viewforth's phase guideline; we think the market will pay less, and the case still works if it does.
Viewforth's phase rule sets NKT's fair 24-month-forward P/E at 30.17x, the 90th percentile of its own ten-year range. We expect the market to pay about 19-20x over 18 months, because that history is inflated by the trough-earnings years of 2019-21 and because EPS growth slows to about 10% after 2028 as new competitors' capacity arrives. Sections #11 and #12 show that the case works at either multiple.
7
The plan: start a position now, add in the spring 2027 dip, and go to full size on first commercial cable.
Start now, because the skew already favours the position and NKT's largest shareholder, BlackRock, raised its stake from 5.94% to 8.46% in October. Add in the likely February-May 2027 dip. Go to full size on confirmed first commercial cable (May-August 2027), when most of the uncertainty falls away. Consider hedging NKT's 0.85 beta to its sector.
Start nowAdd into the February-May 2027 dipFull size on first commercial cable

What would change our mind, and when we would know

19 November 2026 (Q3 results):a Transmission margin below about 17%, or a quarterly working-capital outflow above 300m EUR.
February 2027 (FY2027 guidance):a FY2027 EBITDA range below 480m EUR, or a later commissioning date.
May-August 2027:no first commercial cable from the new lines.
From Q3 2027:a margin on the new lines' first kilometres well below the margin on the existing lines.
Any time from 2027:a European 525kV contract won by a new entrant at a visibly lower price.

#1Operating environment: contracted tailwinds drive the earnings, and the headwinds act on the multiple

NKT's operating environment runs on two clocks. Contracted tailwinds set NKT's 2027-28 earnings. The headwinds act on the valuation: the market regime sets the multiple over the next 6-12 months, and competitors' new capacity, which catches up with demand around 2029-30, sets the terminal value. The earnings carry the case; the multiple is the swing factor.

European grid demand is structural, legally mandated and already converted into signed contracts.

NKT's Q1 2026 order intake was a record 4.2bn EUR, including Eastern Green Link 3 at 2.2bn, its largest award ever. Beyond the 13.0bn EUR backlog sit more than 2.5bn EUR of further TenneT awards and about 2.5bn of capacity bookings, and orders placed across the industry in Q1 2026 are for delivery in 2031-32. Capacity, not demand, limits NKT's revenue to 2029.

European policy is raising the barriers to entry as well as extending demand. Germany's draft Offshore Wind Act caps Chinese components; the UK's record 8.4 GW contract-for-difference auction rewards local supply chains; and the EU's Net-Zero Industry Act effectively excludes Chinese makers from most grid tenders. Each measure strengthens the three qualified European incumbents: Prysmian, Nexans and NKT.

Competition cannot turn into a price war before 2028, because no cable maker has spare capacity. A new plant takes three to five years to build and a cable-laying vessel about three, and the industry's order books are sold out to 2029-30. Transmission margins are rising at all three incumbents at once (Q2 2026: Prysmian 21.2%, NKT 20.2%, Nexans 13.7%).

The headwinds act on the multiple and the terminal value, not on the 2027-28 earnings.

  • The market regime is the strongest headwind over the next six months. Viewforth's market reading of 9 October describes a late-cycle rates squeeze turning into European credit and sovereign stress (French bonds 152bp over German, market breadth at three-year lows). In this regime investors pay for visible cash and penalise long-dated projects. NKT's negative free cash flow until 2027 therefore depresses its multiple, not its EPS.
  • New capacity catches up with demand around 2029-30. Sumitomo, LS Cable, Taihan and Hellenic Cables are building or newly qualified, and the incumbents are adding about 30%. Morgan Stanley expects parity by 2030, and 15% oversupply if European offshore wind installs only 13 GW a year. In the last cycle prices fell steeply at parity, and NKT lost money at EBIT level in 2019-20.
  • Input costs are a mild headwind. NKT has no in-house metal processing and does not index polymer or ship-fuel costs; the Strait of Hormuz feedstock shock cost Distribution about one point of margin in Q2 2026. Transmission passes metal costs through.
  • Fragile offshore-wind developers are not NKT's customers. NKT contracts with the grid operators that own the connections.
Bgrade
Score: 78. Demand, price and the local-content barrier are contracted or legislated through 2028, which places NKT's operating environment near the top of European listed companies. The two real headwinds, the discount rate and capacity parity around 2030, act on the multiple rather than on the earnings Richard is underwriting.
FDCBA

#2Internal change forces: one large, funded, physical change, run by a stretched organisation

NKT's internal change is a single, dated capacity step: about 2bn EUR of capital expenditure over 2025-28.
Karlskrona, Sweden:a third extrusion tower (Crown, 200 metres) with two new extrusion lines makes this the world's largest offshore high-voltage cable site. Commercial operation is due in Q2 2027, "slightly ahead of the original schedule"; full volume in 2028.
Cologne, Germany:a 100m EUR onshore cable expansion, due in 2027.
Vessels:the cable-laying vessel Eleonora (first campaign in H2 2027), plus a barge and a trencher in 2027.
Testing and medium voltage:a 640kV test hall, and expansions that add about 40% to Distribution capacity.

Every Karlskrona milestone has been met so far, and the start-up date has just moved earlier. The tower was built in late 2024, the machinery has been in commissioning tests since Q1 2026, and about 85% of the assets are "out of the ground". A company six months from start-up that brings its date forward is sending the strongest signal available short of the start-up itself.

NKT's price rises are already written into its contracts and reach the income statement automatically. Contract values per kilometre have risen 2.3 times since 2019-20, a real increase of roughly 15% a year, and the Transmission margin rose from 15.3% to 20.2% in the year to Q2 2026 while carrying up to 200bp of start-up costs.

NKT's leadership offers engineering continuity, but the organisation shows strain.

  • CEO Claes Westerlind is a former ABB HVDC engineer who ran Karlskrona: the right profile for a plant start-up.
  • The CFO left in April 2026 as a "bad leaver", and his successor comes from strategy and M&A rather than treasury. Two operational executive vice-presidents also left during the ramp-up year.
  • NKT's only capital-budget failure on record was a 300m EUR (about 40%) overrun at Karlskrona, disclosed in December 2024.

The narrowness of NKT's change is an advantage, because the path from capacity to earnings is short and datable. NKT has no cost programme, no acquisition step-up and no large new market.

Organisational strain is the one loop that could link NKT's risks together, so we treat it as raising the odds of the downside scenario rather than as a separate risk.

Cgrade
Score: 66. A large, dated, fully funded change, with a clean milestone record so far and real price rises already in the backlog. The score is held below the top quartile by the narrowness of the change, one past capital-budget failure, and an organisation visibly running near its limit during the ramp-up.
FDCBA

#3Value chain, industry structure, business model, financial profile and management: a protected oligopoly until about 2030

The high-voltage cable industry is as supportive as an industrial structure gets, until about 2030. Three qualified makers hold roughly three-quarters of qualified European supply. Four barriers protect them:

Qualification:years of type testing for each voltage class.
Physical capacity:plants and vessels take three to five years to build.
Regulation:EU resilience criteria favour European makers.
Track record:grid operators book capacity "strictly on track record".

The customers are regulated monopolies that now pay deposits to secure capacity: NKT holds 1.9bn EUR of customer prepayments, and its net working capital is -36% of revenue. In the sector's own words, the incumbents "have kept the whole scarcity rent".

NKT is the best placed of the three incumbents until 2030 and the most exposed after that.

Strengths

  • The second-largest backlog on a third of the leader's capacity.
  • First to 525kV extruded HVDC cable and to 640kV testing.
  • A single-site cost advantage.
  • A turnkey offer: own vessels, accessories and installation.
  • A tender win rate above 30% even as prices more than doubled.

Weaknesses

  • The smallest: Prysmian's Transmission revenue is about 2.6 times NKT's.
  • Two vessels and a barge, against Prysmian's eight by 2028.
  • No plant outside Europe and no in-house metal processing.
  • One main site concentrates the risk as well as the cost advantage.

These barriers belong to the oligopoly rather than to NKT alone. They protect NKT's share and margin through 2028, but they will not protect prices once capacity catches up with demand.

Transmission is the engine; NKT's other two segments matter less. Distribution (about 35% of standard revenue, at a 10.4-11% margin) is fragmented, cyclical and a price-taker. Grid Solutions and Accessories (about 15% margin) grows with the installed cable base and with repairs after sabotage in the Baltic.

NKT's financial profile is the strongest of its peer group and improving fast, yet its multiple sits lowest in its own range.

Two caveats apply. NKT's headline return on capital of 24% is flattered by customer prepayments: DNB Carnegie's adjusted return on invested capital is 8.4%, because about 1.5bn EUR of capital is not yet producing, and it rises toward 15-16% by FY2028-29. Free cash flow is negative until 2027, for the reasons in #5.

NKT's management are strong engineers with an excellent profit record, a weaker record on capital and cash, and governance that has kept pace rather than led.

Profit record:initial guidance beaten by 9-27% in each of the last four years, and the Champlain Hudson project delivered ahead of target.
Strategy:right for scarcity (sell capacity before building it, make customers fund it), but with no hedge against capacity parity.
Governance gaps:a non-independent chair since 2006, no internal audit function, and live antitrust cases in four countries, with fines likely in the low tens of millions of euros.
Cgrade
Score: 68. An oligopoly with high barriers to entry, a business model whose next three years are contracted, a financial profile set to move from "becoming strong" to "strong" in FY2028, and capable engineering management. The score is held back from the top tier by single-site concentration, the absence of a barrier that survives capacity parity, and management and governance that are weaker on capital and cash than on profit.
FDCBA

#4Guidance: conservative by habit, raised every year, and about to produce a misleading headline

NKT's guidance record is among the most consistent in the Viewforth universe. NKT has raised its EBITDA range during every year since FY2022, and each outcome has beaten the midpoint of the first range by 9-27%. The habit is deliberate: repair windfalls are excluded and start-up costs are included in full. Jefferies calls it "setting highly beatable targets".

NKT's mid-term ambitions are stale floors that are more likely to be raised than missed.

80%
2028: EBITDA above 700m EUR (consensus 754m, our model 730m). Even a two-quarter slip gives about 690m, so we put the probability of meeting it at about 80%.
45%
2030: EBITDA above 900m EUR (consensus 936-940m; DNB Carnegie 1.1-1.3bn). We put the probability of a raise within 18 months at 45%.
The catch: NKT's next guidance event will look like a cut. In February 2027 NKT will publish its first FY2027 range, and we expect a midpoint 5-12% below consensus: 495-545m EUR against about 560m (75% probability). Headlines will read "guidance below consensus". The market's reaction is the risk: after the August 2026 raise, the shares still fell 6.7% over three months.
15-20%
The probability of a genuine guidance cut over 18 months is about 15-20%, and only a later commissioning date could cause one. Demand, price and metal costs cannot cause a cut within the horizon.
Richard should treat the February 2027 range as a floor and the likely share-price weakness as a buying opportunity. On NKT's record, a range of 490-540m EUR points to an outcome of about 540-580m. The one item in that announcement that would change the case is the commissioning date.
Cgrade
Score: 74. One of the most conservative and reliable guidance records in European equities, with mid-term ambitions more likely to be raised than missed. The score loses points because the market no longer rewards the beats and because the next guidance event will produce a negative headline before the pattern pays off.
FDCBA

#5Revenue growth leading to outsized profit growth: revenue up 36% lifts EPS 94% from FY2026 to FY2028

NKT's profit growth in FY2027-28 is outsized and contracted, but it is a dated step rather than a compounding engine. On our model, standard revenue growth of 13% and 21% produces EPS growth of 33% and 45%. From FY2029 profit growth slows to a normal 10-15%.

Two forces already in the contracts lift the margin. Newer, higher-priced contracts add about 150-200bp a year to the Transmission margin, and the shift in mix toward Transmission (from about 52% to 62% of revenue by FY2029, at twice Distribution's margin) adds a further 120-150bp to the group margin.

Operating leverage is about to work in NKT's favour for the first time since the build began. The incremental margin on new Transmission revenue is about 35-40%, because the low-margin subcontracted work on the Champlain Hudson project has ended, the crews for the new lines are already on the payroll, and the new kilometres carry the newer prices.

Depreciation nearly doubles, from 121m EUR in FY2025 to about 205-240m by FY2028-29, so EBIT grows more slowly than EBITDA.

Financial leverage adds nothing, but nothing dilutes EPS either. NKT keeps net cash of 430-930m EUR throughout FY2026-29, and the share count, up 59% over 2019-23, stays flat.

NKT's real leverage is its 1.9bn EUR of customer prepayments, which behave like debt in reverse. Customers paid cash up front to fund the build, and NKT now repays them in cable. That repayment is why free cash flow lags earnings until FY2028.

NKT has no cost lever, by design. Only 3-5% of its costs are discretionary, so each quarter of lost production would cost 40-50m EUR of EBITDA in full.

Cgrade
Score: 74. Proven pricing power, high operating leverage that is just starting to work, and reinforcing feedback loops make NKT one of the strongest earnings-gearing set-ups in the universe for 2027-28. The score is held below the top decile because the gearing is a one-off step with an end date, cost control offers no defence, and financial leverage adds nothing.
FDCBA

#6Forecast financials: EPS nearly doubles in two years, at the highest margins in NKT's history

NKT's growth is assured in direction, and the level is high. On our model, EPS compounds at about 24% a year from a tax-normalised FY2025 base of about 4.0 EUR to 7.67 EUR in FY2028. The group EBITDA margin reaches about 20% of standard revenue by FY2028, the highest in NKT's history, and it rests on contracted prices rather than a cyclical peak.

Our model differs from consensus by less than it first appears.

  • timingEBITDA, 1-4% below consensus: the FY2027 increase is weighted to H2 2027, and the margin on the new lines' first kilometres builds gradually.
  • mostly timingEPS, 3-5% below in FY2027-28: on management's own pointers for depreciation, tax and the hybrid-bond coupon, only 2-4 points of the gap are structural.
  • genuine disagreementFY2027 free cash flow: the sell-side calls the working-capital outflow "temporary"; we see a multi-year unwind of prepayments. We put FY2027 at about zero, against +83m EUR in consensus.
  • consensus too lowFY2029 free cash flow: consensus of 306m EUR looks too low.

The range of outcomes is narrow for FY2026, wide and skewed down for FY2027, and centred on 730m EUR for FY2028. FY2027 carries the real uncertainty because a one-quarter slip costs 40-50m EUR of EBITDA and the start-up date can slip but cannot come forward.

Three sources of upside are in no one's numbers.

A third extrusion line in the Crown tower:about 90m EUR of capital expenditure for 70-80m EUR of EBITDA. We put a decision within 18 months at 25-35%.
Licence royalties from Taiwan:expected from about Q3 2027.
Share buybacks from 2029:at one times EBITDA of leverage, NKT could return about 1.7bn EUR by end-2029.
Bgrade
Score: 82. Contracted EPS growth of 33% and 45% in FY2027-28 at record margins, with net cash and a new dividend, places NKT in the top fifth of European companies for forecast growth. The score is not higher because the growth is a two-year step that slows to about 10% from FY2029 and because cash lags earnings.
FDCBA

#7Scope for upgrades to guidance, estimates and the narrative over the next 6-12 months: cuts first, upgrades from August 2027

There is no hidden under-estimation to exploit, so NKT's upgrade story is about timing, not level. Sell-side EBITDA estimates already sit at or above our model, Jefferies 5-9% above consensus. The brokers with full models already describe most of the dynamics we tested.

The likely path of revisions over the next 12 months has its low point in spring 2027.

Genuine upgrades can come from five sources, in order of likelihood: the August 2027 guidance raise; a raise of the stale 2030 ambition (45%); upgrades of more than 5% to FY2029-30 estimates (45%, against 20% for cuts of that size); a decision on a third extrusion line; and the dividend, which FactSet consensus still shows as zero for FY2026-27.

Spring 2027 is the entry point, because estimates, revision breadth and the share price are all likely to sit below today's levels at the same time. The 6-12 month window holds both halves of the sequence, so net upgrade scope over 12 months is small.
Dgrade
Score: 46. Over the next 6-12 months the sell-side is more likely to trim its EPS and cash-flow estimates than to raise them, so near-term upgrade scope is below average. Scope opens from August 2027 through the guidance raise, the stale 2030 ambition and the unmodelled third line.
FDCBA

#8Current momentum: estimates up, share price down

NKT's estimates and its share price are moving in opposite directions, and that divergence is the story of the stock today.

NKT's peers have stronger earnings momentum and fuller multiples. NKT's six-month FY2028 upgrade is the weakest of the four, because its estimates were already high and its revenue is capped by capacity.

NKT's low multiple is its own, so NKT's own milestones can re-rate it. About 45% of NKT's daily price variance comes from the sector (beta 0.85), but NKT has been de-rated inside a re-rated sector. A sector sell-off can still pull the shares down whatever happens at Karlskrona.
Dgrade
Score: 48. Strong guidance and estimate momentum is offset by a technically weak share price, slowing revisions and peers whose momentum sits in their multiples rather than in NKT's favour. NKT is in the middle of the universe today, and a turn in its price momentum depends on its own evidence in 2027.
FDCBA

#9Riskiness and simplicity of the case: one driver, one site, one date

75-80%
The case is simple: one driver, one site, one date. About 75-80% of NKT's FY2025-28 EBITDA increase depends on the new capacity at Karlskrona, Cologne and the Eleonora vessel. Demand, price and input costs, which cause most industrial forecast errors, are contracted, indexed or passed through.

A commissioning slip is the dominant risk, and it can be tracked on known dates.

"Delivered" and "missed" will coexist, and Richard should expect both headlines. NKT has about a 70% chance of delivering our 18-month EBITDA within 10%, but only about a 30% chance of meeting FY2027 consensus EPS.

NKT's risks are correlated, so the downside should be modelled as one branch. A strained organisation that slips on commissioning is also more likely to suffer a vessel or project incident in the same period.

The uncertainty collapses on known dates, which makes the case unusually tractable for position sizing. The range of outcomes roughly halves at each of 19 November 2026, February 2027 and May-August 2027.

Cgrade
Score: 60. Simple, contracted and highly trackable, with a downside that is mainly a delay and that resolves on known dates. The score is held to the upper-middle because the case hangs on one binary event at one site, cash flow is poorly disclosed, and the multiple is exposed to sector and market-regime moves that NKT cannot control.
FDCBA

#10Where the stock is in its lifecycle: reinforcing fundamentals, stalled share price

NKT's fundamentals are in the "Reinforcing" phase while its share price has stalled. We read the stall as a mid-cycle pause, not the start of a "Stalling" phase.

The market is pricing capacity parity in 2029-30 two to three years early. Investors have historically de-rated cable makers as soon as new capacity is announced, years before prices fall, and today's market regime amplifies that habit. A genuine "Stalling" phase needs the fundamentals to stall, and on our model they do not stall until FY2029.

The phase argues for owning NKT now, before the thesis visibly broadens, but against paying a peak multiple until the forecasts are confirmed in August 2027.
Cgrade
Score: 62. A fundamentally reinforcing case in a temporary price stall, with a dated catalyst that should move it into the "thesis broadening" phase within about 10 months, which ranks it above the median European stock. A further dip into spring 2027 is likely before the turn.
FDCBA

#11Fair multiple: the guideline says 30.17x; we think the market will pay about 19-20x

Viewforth's phase guideline sets NKT's fair 24-month-forward P/E at 30.17x, which implies a re-rating of 84% from today's 16.4x. For a "Reinforcing" stock, the guideline takes the 90th percentile of its own ten-year P/E history as fair, with the 80th (26.35x) as the bear case and the 95th (33.74x) as the bull case.

We think the guideline is mechanically right but economically too high, for four reasons.

1Trough earnings distort NKT's history.In 2019-20 EPS was near zero and the P/E read up to 178x. The 90th percentile prices a recovery from losses, not a contracted earnings step.
2NKT's peers trade lower.Prysmian trades at 17.2x, Cenergy at 15.8x and Nexans at 12.2x. At 30x, NKT would trade at about 1.75 times Prysmian, which has more diversified growth.
3NKT's growth is a step.EPS growth of 33% and 45% in FY2027-28 slows to about 10% from FY2029, when a harvesting business deserves a mid-to-high-teens multiple.
4The terminal risk is dated.Capacity parity in 2029-30, and the 2016-20 price collapse at parity, cap what a rational buyer will pay for 2030 earnings.

Our fair multiple of 19-20x over 18 months is NKT's ten-year median, reached once the plant runs, free cash flow turns and a dividend is paid. A multiple of 19-20x implies about 10 times FY2029 enterprise value to EBITDA, close to the 10.7 times FY2027 at which Prysmian trades today. Over three years we expect 16-18x, with upside to 20x if the 2028 capital-markets event sets out a credible second phase of growth.

The guideline's 30x would be right only if the market came to believe that scarcity lasts well beyond 2030. Lasting scarcity is DNB Carnegie's view, with 2030 EBITDA of 1.1-1.3bn EUR, and we do not make it our base case. The memo's fair multiple remains the guideline's 30.17x; #12 shows the returns at our view beside it.
Cgrade
Score: 70. At 15.9x, the 21st percentile of its range, and a PEG ratio (P/E divided by EPS growth) of about 0.5, the lowest growth-adjusted multiple among its peers, NKT trades far below the guideline's 30.17x and below even our more cautious 19-20x for the next 18 months. Valuation support of that size places NKT in the upper third of European stocks. The score is not higher because a dated 2030 overhang caps the fair multiple itself.
FDCBA

#13Summary conclusion: buy in stages, because the 2027 start-up decides the outcome and the market has not priced it

NKT is a rare inflection case: its demand, prices and costs are already contracted, so the investment question reduces to one dated, observable event, the start-up of two new lines at Karlskrona around Q2 2027. If the lines start on time, EBITDA rises about 70% in two years, EPS nearly doubles and free cash flow turns positive. The market values NKT at the 21st percentile of its own range and has chosen to wait.

The market's wait is the opportunity, and the expected order of events shows Richard how to use it. The next six months will probably look bad on paper, with a "below consensus" guidance range and trimmed estimates, but none of that changes the destination. From August 2027 first commercial cable, a likely guidance raise and positive free cash flow arrive. The 18-month return is about +128% at the fair multiple and about +28% probability-weighted at ours, with a 5% chance of losing 16-27%.

Recommendation: buy, in three stages

Consider pairing the position against a basket of sector peers to neutralise NKT's 0.85 sector beta while the peers' multiples sit near the top of their ranges.

The checkpoints that confirm the case

19 November 2026:a Transmission margin of 19% or more, and a quarterly working-capital outflow below 300m EUR.
February 2027:a FY2027 EBITDA range of 490m EUR or more, with the Q2 2027 start-up date confirmed.
May-August 2027:first commercial cable from the new lines.
November 2027:a Q3 Transmission margin heading to 23-24%.
Throughout:contract prices on European 525kV tenders holding up.
If those checkpoints are met, NKT is the stock to own into 2028. Reassess at the 2028 capital-markets event, when NKT must show whether it has a second phase of growth after the harvest.

End notes

  1. Dates and bases. Share price 867 DKK on 12 October 2026, converted at 7.46 DKK per euro. Consensus is the FactSet median of 25 September 2026. Latest results: Q2/H1 2026 (13 August 2026); Investor Day 29 September 2026.
  2. Revenue and EBITDA. Revenue and margins are at standard metal prices (NKT's basis) unless marked "reported"; reported revenue includes copper and aluminium passed through to customers, about 1.35-1.39 times standard revenue, which inflates reported growth and leaves EBITDA unchanged. EBITDA in the text is NKT's operational EBITDA. EPS is after the hybrid-bond coupon.
  3. Our model and consensus. Our model is Viewforth's base case: operational EBITDA of 424m, 541m, 730m and 830m EUR for FY2026-29 and EPS of 3.96, 5.28, 7.67 and 8.53 EUR. Consensus: 426m, 562m, 754m and 847m EUR, and 4.17, 5.50, 7.90 and 9.54 EUR. The standard charts and the line-by-line table use FactSet history and the brokers' basis, so their figures differ slightly.
  4. The phase guideline. The guideline uses 110 of 116 months of history, excluding 6 outlier months. Today's multiple is 16.4x on its measure and 15.9x on the dashboard's consensus measure.
  5. The Financial Analyst's return table. The table gives +123% to Q4 2027, +129% to Q1 2028 and +154% to Q4 2028 at the fair multiple. Its three parts for Q4 2027 (EPS 37%, multiple 61%, dividends 2%) are shares of the return that sum to 100% against a total of 123%; the 23 missing points are the interaction between earnings growth and re-rating.
  6. An unresolved data point. One source gives NKT's largest customer as 612m EUR (17.2% of 2025 revenue); another says no customer exceeded 10%. The forecasts are unaffected, because more than 95% of the backlog sits with a handful of grid operators.
  7. Terms. HVDC: high-voltage direct current. kV: kilovolt. GW: gigawatt. ENTSO-E: the European Network of Transmission System Operators for Electricity. RIIO-T3: the UK regulator's current price-control period for electricity transmission. Contract for difference: a state contract fixing the price a generator receives. Enterprise value to EBITDA: market value plus net debt, divided by EBITDA.
